message.content:
We're investigating whether Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) product data, as exposed through this PWA Kit project, reliably provides TWO distinct product images (a primary/flat product shot and a second "on model" shot) for every product, or whether a second image is sometimes genuinely absent — needed for a future integration mapping real commerce data onto a Zimmermann-built ZimmProductCardMedia component's `primaryImage`/`hoverImage` props. This is pure research: report facts with exact file:line citations and quoted source, do not write or modify any code, do not guess.

Please investigate and report back:

1. **Type-level evidence**: Look in `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for the Product type's `imageGroups`/`image` shape. Is a second/alternate image guaranteed to exist (e.g. a fixed-cardinality field), or is it an array that could plausibly have length 1? Quote the actual type definition.

2. **Real, already-working precedent**: Search `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/` and `app/components/image-gallery/` (or wherever the base PWA Kit renders product images) for how it handles a product that has only ONE image — does it have any fallback/guard logic (e.g. `images?.[1] ?? images[0]`, an `imageGroups.find(...)` that could return undefined, optional chaining, a conditional hover-swap), or would accessing a "second image" break/throw if absent? Quote the exact code with file path and line numbers.

3. **Our own already-built component**: Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` and its type definitions in this same repo. Is the `hoverImage` prop optional? Trace through the component's render logic — if `hoverImage` is not passed, does it correctly render just `primaryImage` with no swap-related UI (no arrows implying multiple images, no broken hover-swap markup), or does something break/look wrong? Quote the exact relevant lines.

Report back concisely (under 400 words) with the concrete findings and exact citations. If something genuinely cannot be determined from static code/types alone, say so plainly rather than guessing.

18	    let {viewType, selectedVariationAttributes = {}} = options
19	
20	    // Start by filtering out any imageGroup that isn't the correct viewType.
21	    imageGroups = imageGroups.filter(

23	    )
24	
25	    // Not all variation attributes are reflected in images. For example, you probably
26	    // won't have a separate image group for various sizes, but you might for colors. For that
27	    // reason we need to know what are valid attribute values to filter on.
28	    const refinableAttributeIds = [
29	        ...new Set(
30	            imageGroups
31	                .reduce((acc, {variationAttributes = []}) => [...acc, ...variationAttributes], [])
32	                .map(({id}) => id)
33	        )
34	    ]
35	
36	    // Update the `selectedVariationAttributes` by filtering out the attributes that have no
37	    // representation in this imageGroup.
38	    selectedVariationAttributes = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes).reduce((acc, curr) => {
39	        return refinableAttributeIds.includes(curr)
40	            ? {
41	                  ...acc,
42	                  [`${curr}`]: selectedVariationAttributes[curr]
43	              }
44	            : acc
45	    }, {})
46	
47	    // Find the image group that has all the all the selected variation value attributes.
48	    imageGroups = imageGroups.find(({variationAttributes = []}) => {
49	        const selectedIds = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes)
50	
51	        return selectedIds.every((selectedId) => {
52	            const selectedValue = selectedVariationAttributes[selectedId]
53	
54	            return variationAttributes.find(
55	                ({id, values}) =>
56	                    id === selectedId && values.every(({value}) => value === selectedValue)
57	            )
58	        })
59	    })
60	
61	    return imageGroups

Type-level evidence** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` - Line 32760-32774, `Product.imageGroups?: Array` — the whole array is optional. - Line 32625-32631: `type ImageGroup = { images: Array; variationAttributes?: Array; viewType: string; } & { [key: string]: any; };` — `images` is a plain `Array`, no tuple/fixed-length typing (e.g. not `[Image, Image]`), so it can legally have length 0 or 1. - Line 32272-32279: `type Image = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link: string; title?: string; } & { [key: string]: any; };` — only `link` is required. **No cardinality guarantee exists anywhere in the type system.** A second image is not type-guaranteed; the array shape permits length 1 (or 0). **2. Real precedent in base PWA Kit** - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:182-205` (`filterImageGroups`) and `.../app/utils/image-groups-utils.js:17-62` (`findImageGroupBy`) both return possibly-`undefined`/empty results and never assume a minimum image count. - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx:129`: `return filteredImageGroups?.[0]?.images[0]` — optional chaining guards the group lookup; only `images[0]` is ever read. **ProductTile has no hover-swap feature and never touches a second image at all** (confirmed: no `hover`/`swap` matches anywhere in that file). - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/image-gallery/index.jsx:98-99`: `const heroImage = heroImageGroup?.images?.[selectedIndex]` and `const thumbnailImages = thumbnailImageGroup?.images || []` — fully optional-chained/defaulted; line 106 further guards render with `{heroImage && (...)}`. Nothing in either file accesses a fixed "second image" index or would throw if only one image exists — accessing `images[1]` on a 1-length array simply yields `undefined` in JS, never a runtime error. **3. Our own component** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` - Line 48: `hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardMediaImage;` — optional. - Line 120-124: `const gallery = images && images.length > 1 ? images : undefined; const slideImages = gallery ?? [primaryImage]; ... const showHoverSwap = swapOnHover && Boolean(hoverImage) && !gallery;` — if `hoverImage` is absent, `showHoverSwap` is `false`. - Line 220 (`if (isPrimaryPosition && showHoverSwap && hoverImage)`) then falls through to the plain single-`` branch (lines 241-250); `canPage` (line 124) and the `totalSlides > 1` indicator gate (line 287) are both false, so no arrows/indicator render. - Confirmed by the component's own test suite, `index.test.tsx:128-133`: `describe('... single image renders no paging affordance' ...) test('renders no arrow buttons and no slide indicator, even when showControls is true' ...) expect(screen.queryAllByRole('button')).toHaveLength(0); expect(screen.queryByRole('group')).not.toBeInTheDocument();` **Conclusion**: Nothing in the type definitions, the base PWA Kit's rendering code, or our own component guarantees or requires two images. A second image is a plain, optional array element that can genuinely be absent, and both the upstream code and our `ZimmProductCardMedia` degrade cleanly (primary-image-only, no broken markup) when it is. Whether SFCC's *actual merchandised catalog data* always populates two images per product is a content/business-process question, not something determinable from static code or types — that would require inspecting live/sample API responses, which is outside this codebase.
